mainTopic: The height of the טבילה room, the linen sheet, the כהן גדול's first טבילה and the morning תמיד, and the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן over קידוש ידיים ורגליים
overview: The amud opens by finishing a calculation from the previous amud. That calculation found the water of עין עיטם to be 23 אמות above the עזרה: a 20-אמה gate plus a 3-אמה מקוה on top. The גמרא asks why the ceiling and plaster were not added in. It answers that the marble layers were very thin, and anything under a full אמה is not counted. Next it explains that the modesty sheet was made of בוץ to remind the כהן גדול that the day's special service is done in linen. A new משנה then describes the כהן גדול's first טבילה, his change into בגדי זהב, and the morning תמיד, including when the קטורת is offered. It also allows warming the מקוה for an old or delicate כהן גדול. In the גמרא, רב פפא explains the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about when the קידוש ידיים ורגליים for removing garments is done. A ברייתא then shows that רבי מאיר requires a קידוש even at the first change of clothes, and רב פפא retracts. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a challenge to the רבנן about the משנה's count of קידושים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ceiling and plaster should add two more cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 23-אמה total, since the ceiling and the plaster layer should each add an אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also an אמה for the ceiling and an אמה for the plaster floor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier math. If the gate is 20 אמות and the מקוה on top is 3 אמות, we have forgotten the ceiling and the floor between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standard ceiling (תקרה) and the plaster layer over it (מעזיבה) are each normally an אמה thick. That would make the total at least 25 אמות, not the 23 in the earlier calculation.

keyTerms.meaning: Plaster or packed-earth layer laid over the ceiling

phrases.english: But there is a cubit of ceiling
phrases.notes: That's the thickness of the ceiling over the gate.

phrases.english: and a cubit of plaster!
phrases.notes: That's the thickness of the plaster floor of the מקוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא אַמָּה תִּקְרָה וְאַמָּה מַעֲזִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous daf's calculation of 20 + 3 = 23 אמות
steps.kashyaTarget: The calculation that the water of עין עיטם was exactly 23 אמות above the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Standard construction adds an אמה of ceiling and an אמה of plaster, which brings the total to 25.

steps.title: The Temple gates were marble and built thin
steps.stepSummary: The gates of the בית המקדש were made of marble, so their ceilings and plaster were built with only minimal thickness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The gates of the בית המקדש were made of marble, so they built them with only a tiny thickness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the full-אמה rule does not apply here. Marble is strong, so a thin layer was enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה-thick ceiling is normal for ordinary building materials. Marble (שישא) is strong, so the ceiling and plaster were only a משהו. That removes the extra two אמות.

phrases.english: The gates of the Temple,
since they are marble,
they made them with a minimal amount.
phrases.notes: In other words, the ceiling and the plaster were made very thin.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁעָרִים דְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ כֵּיוָן דְּשֵׁישָׁא נִינְהוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the building material was different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ceiling and plaster were a standard full אמה each
steps.terutzMaskana: Because they were marble, they were only a minimal thickness

steps.title: Even a minimal thickness still adds something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses: even a thin layer adds some height beyond 23 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still that small amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Thin or not, the ceiling still has some thickness, so the total should be a little over 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer removed the full two אמות but not the small leftover. If the calculation means exactly 23, the extra bit seems to be ignored.

phrases.english: But there is that minimal amount!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the marble layers were only a משהו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משהו is still something, so the height should be more than exactly 23 אמות.

steps.title: Less than a full cubit is not counted
steps.stepSummary: Since the extra thickness is not a full אמה, it was not included in the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it was not a whole אמה, he does not count it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the extra bit exists. The calculation simply counted only in whole אמות and ignored the small fraction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not deny the extra thickness. It explains that the measurement was given in round numbers, so a fraction of an אמה was left out. This closes the height discussion.
steps.whatToRemember: The 23 אמות are 20 for the gate plus 3 for the מקוה. The marble ceiling was thin, and anything under a full אמה is left out of the count.

phrases.english: since it was not a whole cubit —
he does not count it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הֲוַאי אַמְּתָא לָא חָשֵׁיב לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 and ends the height discussion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every bit of thickness must be included in the total
steps.terutzMaskana: Only whole אמות are counted, so the minimal thickness is ignored

steps.title: Why was the modesty sheet made of linen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about spreading a linen sheet and asks why it had to be linen specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They spread a sheet of linen.' Why specifically linen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves back to an earlier line of the משנה and asks a clarifying question. Any sheet would give privacy, so why does the משנה insist on linen?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheet only served modesty while the כהן גדול undressed and went into the מקוה. Since the material does not seem to matter for that job, the specific mention of בוץ needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why specifically this?

phrases.english: 'They spread a sheet of fine linen, etc.'
Why specifically of linen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns to a phrase in the earlier משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the משנה requires the sheet to be made of linen

steps.title: Linen reminds him the day's service is in linen
steps.stepSummary: Using רב כהנא's reasoning, the linen sheet reminds the כהן גדול that the special service of יום הכיפורים is done in linen garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב כהנא said, so that he will realize that the service of the day is done in linen garments. Here too, the linen sheet is so that he will realize the service of the day is in linen garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא borrows a reason רב כהנא gave in a related case and applies it to the sheet. The linen is a visual reminder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main עבודת היום of יום הכיפורים is done in בגדי לבן made of linen. Even though the כהן גדול is about to put on בגדי זהב, the linen sheet reminds him of the day's central service. The phrase הכא נמי shows the reason is being transferred from רב כהנא's case to this one.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he will recognize / be aware
The special service of the day (יום הכיפורים)

steps.confusionAlert: The sheet is not one of the כהן גדול's garments. It only screens him from the people, yet its material still carries a message about the day.

phrases.english: As Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּכִּיר שֶׁעֲבוֹדַת הַיּוֹם בְּבִגְדֵי בוּץ.
phrases.english: so that he will be aware that the service of the day is in linen garments.
Here too: so that he will be aware
that the service of the day is in linen garments.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The linen sheet serves as a reminder that the day's main service is done in linen garments, applying רב כהנא's reasoning.

steps.title: משנה: first immersion, golden garments, and the morning תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes the כהן גדול immersing, putting on בגדי זהב, washing hands and feet, and doing the slaughter, receiving, and sprinkling of the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He undressed, went down and immersed, came up and dried himself. They brought him golden garments, he put them on, and he washed his hands and feet. They brought him the תמיד; he cut most of the slaughter, another כהן finished the slaughter for him, and he received the blood and sprinkled it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lays out step by step the start of the כהן גדול's service on יום הכיפורים morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול makes the cut (קרצו), but another כהן completes the שחיטה. This frees the כהן גדול to receive the blood right away, since קבלה is part of the עבודה that he must do himself. Before starting the service he does קידוש ידים ורגלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
The eight golden garments of the כהן גדול
Washed his hands and feet from the כיור
He cut it (made most of the slaughter cut)

steps.confusionAlert: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול does the regular daily service (תמיד) in בגדי זהב. Only the special עבודת היום is done in linen.

phrases.english: MISHNA: He undressed, went down, and immersed,
came up and dried himself.
They brought him golden garments, and he put them on,
and he sanctified his hands and feet.
They brought him the daily offering; he cut it,
and another completed the slaughter for him.
He received the blood and sprinkled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה continuing the order of the יום הכיפורים service
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול immerses, wears בגדי זהב, washes, cuts the תמיד (another כהן finishes the cut), and he receives and sprinkles the blood.

steps.title: משנה: incense, lamps, limbs, griddle-cakes, and wine
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול enters the היכל to offer the morning קטורת and prepare the lamps, then offers the head, limbs, חביתין, and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went in to burn the morning incense and to prepare the lamps, and to offer the head, the limbs, the griddle-cakes, and the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues listing the rest of the morning service, all done by the כהן גדול himself on this day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a normal day these jobs are split among many כהנים. On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול does them all personally. The list covers inside work (קטורת, נרות) and outside work on the מזבח (limbs, חביתין, נסכים).

keyTerms.meaning: To clean and prepare the lamps of the מנורה
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake meal offering

phrases.english: He entered to burn the morning incense,
and to prepare the lamps,
and to offer the head and the limbs
and the griddle-cakes and the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of the morning service
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול personally does the morning קטורת, the הטבת הנרות, and the offering of the limbs, חביתין, and wine.

steps.title: משנה: when the morning and afternoon incense is offered
steps.stepSummary: The משנה notes that the morning קטורת comes between the blood and the limbs, and the afternoon קטורת comes between the limbs and the נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The morning incense was offered between the blood and the limbs. The afternoon incense was offered between the limbs and the libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a timing rule that places the קטורת within the order of the תמיד service, morning and afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the morning the קטורת comes earlier, right after the blood and before the limbs. In the afternoon it comes later, after the limbs and before the wine. This explains why in our משנה the incense appears in the middle of the תמיד's steps.
steps.whatToRemember: Morning: blood → קטורת → limbs. Afternoon: limbs → קטורת → נסכים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sequence explains the order the משנה just listed, and it is the basis for later discussion of the afternoon service on יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: The morning incense was offered
between the blood and the limbs;
that of the afternoon
between the limbs and the libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְטוֹרֶת שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיְתָה קְרֵיבָה בֵּין דָּם לְאֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies where the קטורת from step 8 fits in the order of the service
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Morning קטורת is offered between the blood and the limbs; afternoon קטורת is offered between the limbs and the נסכים.

steps.title: Warming the מקוה for an old or delicate כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the כהן גדול is old or delicate, hot water is added to the cold מקוה to soften its chill.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן גדול was old or delicate, they would heat hot water for him and pour it into the cold water so that the cold would be eased.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more detail about the כהן גדול's immersions. If the cold water is hard on him because he is old or sensitive, they warm the מקוה a little.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hot water is heated ahead of time (ערב יום הכיפורים) and mixed into the cold מקוה. This does not ruin the טבילה. It only takes the edge off the cold so he can immerse without suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: So that their chill is eased

phrases.english: If the High Priest was old
or delicate
they heat hot water for him,
and pour it into the cold water
phrases.notes: Into the cold water of the מקוה

phrases.english: so that its chill is eased.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל זָקֵן אוֹ אִיסְטְנִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's description of the כהן גדול's immersions with a special arrangement for comfort.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hot water may be added to the cold מקוה for an old or delicate כהן גדול to ease the chill.

steps.title: The משנה seems not to follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of the study hall (רבנן) tell רב פפא that the משנה, which mentions only one קידוש, cannot follow רבי מאיר, who requires two קידושים at each change of garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב פפא: This משנה does not follow רבי מאיר. If it did, then since he says two washings of hands and feet are done at each dressing, here too he should do two washings at the dressing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins. Some scholars point out a problem: the משנה describes only one washing of hands and feet when the כהן גדול puts on the gold garments, but רבי מאיר says there should be two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהן גדול immersed, put on בגדי זהב, and then did קידוש ידיים ורגליים once. רבי מאיר holds that every change of garments needs two קידושים. So these scholars (not the רבנן who argue with רבי מאיר) conclude that the משנה must be following the other opinion and not רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages said it before him
This does not follow (a certain opinion)
Washings (sanctifications) of the hands and feet from the כיור

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'קידוש' does not mean the שבת קידוש over wine. It means washing the hands and feet from the כיור before doing עבודה.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages said before Rav Pappa:
This [mishna] is not like Rabbi Meir.
For if it were Rabbi Meir,
since he said two sanctifications
are done for each donning —
here too let him perform
two sanctifications upon the donning!
phrases.notes: But the משנה mentions only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by testing which opinion the משנה follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה could match רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר requires two קידושים per change of garments. The משנה lists only one, so it cannot be his view.

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees to two washings when changing garments
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that both sides agree there is one קידוש for removing holy garments and one for putting them on. Their argument is about something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: According to both the רבנן and רבי מאיר, there is one washing for taking off holy garments and one for putting on. Here, this is what they argue about:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the idea that the משנה goes against רבי מאיר. He explains that the 'two washings' belong to taking off and putting on, and he sets up the real point of the argument, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two קידושים are needed only when the כהן גדול takes off one set of holy garments and puts on another. At the very first dressing of the day he takes off nothing holy, so even רבי מאיר needs only one. That is why the משנה fits everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Both according to the רבנן and according to רבי מאיר
This is what they argue about

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue about whether there are two washings. Both agree there are two at a change of garments. They argue only about when the first one happens.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
Both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Meir
there is one upon removal of sacred garments,
and one upon donning,
and here, this is what they disagree about:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פָּפָּא: בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן בֵּין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the claim in step 11 by redefining what the two קידושים are for.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the opinion: the two קידושים are linked to removal and donning, not two for donning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר requires two קידושים for every donning, even the first one of the day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both opinions require one קידוש for removal and one for donning. At the first dressing nothing holy is removed, so one is enough, and the משנה fits everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the argument away from 'how many washings' to 'when the washing for undressing happens,' which the next two steps explain.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: wash after taking off the garments
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק, רבי מאיר compares removing to donning: just as one dresses and then washes, one undresses and then washes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And he shall remove, and wash, and put on.' רבי מאיר holds: the Torah compares removing to donning. Just as with donning, he puts on and afterward washes, so with removing, he takes off and afterward washes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא now explains רבי מאיר's side of the argument, based on a פסוק that puts taking off and putting on side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא ט״ז) lists removing and putting on together, so the Torah treats them alike (a היקש). With donning, the קידוש comes after the clothes are on. So רבי מאיר says that with removing, the קידוש also comes after the clothes are off.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall remove, and wash, and put on (ויקרא ט״ז)
Compares (draws a היקש between two things)
And afterward he washes his hands and feet

phrases.english: "And he shall remove, and wash, and put on,"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא ט״ז:כ״ג–כ״ד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
[the verse] compares removal to donning,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְבִישָׁה — לוֹבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: just as with donning — he dons and afterward sanctifies,

phrases.aramaic: אַף פְּשִׁיטָה — פּוֹשֵׁט וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: so too with removal — he removes and afterward sanctifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: מַקִּישׁ פְּשִׁיטָה לִלְבִישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first side of the argument that רב פפא announced in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the קידוש for removing garments is done after they are taken off.

steps.title: The רבנן: wash while still dressed
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the same comparison differently: just as with donning the washing is done while dressed, with removing it is also done while still dressed, before undressing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: the Torah compares removing to donning. Just as with donning, he washes while he is dressed, so with removing, he washes while he is still dressed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes by explaining the רבנן's side. They use the same comparison but focus on a different detail: being dressed while washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same היקש, but each takes a different point from donning. רבי מאיר focuses on the order (wash after the change). The רבנן focus on the state (wash while dressed). So for the רבנן, the 'removal' קידוש happens at the end of the עבודה, before the garments come off.

keyTerms.meaning: He washes (sanctifies) his hands and feet

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, everyone agrees there is one קידוש for removing holy garments and one for putting them on, so the first dressing of the day needs only one. רבי מאיר says the removal קידוש comes after undressing. The רבנן say it comes before undressing, while still dressed. (Step 16 shows רב פפא retracting the first point because of a ברייתא.)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
[the verse] compares removal to donning,
just as with donning — when he is dressed he sanctifies,
so too with removal — when he is dressed he sanctifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the argument, using the same comparison as רבי מאיר in step 13 but drawing a different lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, the קידוש for removing garments is done while still dressed, before taking them off.

steps.title: The Sages challenge רב פפא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of the study hall (רבנן) quote a ברייתא showing that רבי מאיר requires a קידוש even after removing ordinary clothes at the very first טבילה. This contradicts רב פפא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to רב פפא: How can you say that? A ברייתא teaches: They spread a sheet of fine linen between the כהן גדול and the people. He undressed, went down, and immersed. He came up and dried himself. They brought him golden garments, he put them on, and he washed his hands and feet. רבי מאיר says: He undressed and washed his hands and feet, went down and immersed, came up and dried himself. They brought him golden garments, he put them on, and he washed his hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack רב פפא's answer from Step 12 by quoting a ברייתא about the first טבילה of the day. In it, רבי מאיר requires two washings, one after undressing and one after dressing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said there is one קידוש for removing holy garments and one for putting them on. That would mean no קידוש is needed when removing ordinary weekday clothes. But in the ברייתא, רבי מאיר requires a קידוש right after removing ordinary clothes, before the טבילה, so he requires two קידושים even at this first change.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenge from a source)
A sheet of fine linen, held up for privacy
The golden garments, the eight special garments of the כהן גדול
He washed his hands and feet from the כיור

steps.confusionAlert: Compare the two opinions carefully. The first opinion has only ONE washing, after dressing. רבי מאיר adds a washing right after undressing. That added washing is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.english: The Sages said to Rav Pappa:
And can you really say this?
phrases.notes: Can you say רבי מאיר requires only one קידוש at the first change?

phrases.english: But was it not taught in a ברייתא:
They spread a sheet of fine linen
between him and the people,
he undressed, went down, and immersed,
he came up and dried himself.
They brought him golden garments, and he put them on,
and he washed his hands and feet.
phrases.notes: First opinion: only one washing, after dressing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
He undressed and washed his hands and feet,
phrases.notes: The extra washing after removing ordinary clothes.

phrases.english: and went down and immersed,
came up and dried himself,
they brought him golden garments,
and he put them on and washed his hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's explanation of the dispute, given in Steps 12-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי מאיר agrees there is only one קידוש for removing and one for putting on, with none required when removing ordinary clothes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר requiring a קידוש after removing ordinary weekday clothes at the first טבילה. So he does require two קידושים there, against רב פפא's framing.

steps.title: רב פפא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concedes: if a ברייתא teaches this, then it is so, and he withdraws his explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If it was taught, it was taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא does not answer the challenge. He accepts the ברייתא over his own reasoning and gives up his position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's view was based on his own reasoning, not on a source. An explicit ברייתא outweighs reasoning, so he retracts. The challenge from Step 15 stands, and רבי מאיר is understood to require a קידוש at the first change as well.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was taught, it was taught. A formula for conceding to an explicit ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא retracts. רבי מאיר requires a קידוש after undressing even at the first טבילה, when the כהן גדול removes ordinary clothes.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If it was taught, it was taught.
phrases.notes: If a ברייתא clearly says so, I'll drop my view and go with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of Step 15 by conceding.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explicit ברייתא overrides רב פפא's reasoning. רבי מאיר requires two קידושים even at the first change of clothes.

steps.title: Granted that רבי מאיר's view works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question by granting that רבי מאיר's view explains how to reach a certain count. The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי מאיר, this is how you find it…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It first grants that רבי מאיר's view fits the count, and it is about to ask how the רבנן can fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two washings at every change, including the first, רבי מאיר reaches the משנה's count of five טבילות and ten קידושים. The "בשלמא" formula signals that a difficulty for the other view, the רבנן, is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works well (sets up a contrast with a view that has a difficulty)
You find it, you can account for it

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full statement. It is the first half of a question that ends on the next amud.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
that is how you find it
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, probably with the count of ten קידושים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that רבי מאיר requires two קידושים at every change, and moves toward testing the רבנן against the משנה's count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the count of קידושים in the משנה is reached according to each view, after granting that it works for רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן on when the קידוש for removing garments is done, tested against the משנה's count of קידושים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר, who requires a קידוש even at the first change of clothes, reaches the full count in the משנה. The רבנן seem to come up short, and the next amud spells this out.
